info.title: OE Commerce Admin REST API
info.description:
Manage a single OE Commerce store's catalogue, orders, customers, and store configuration from
            your own back-office tooling. Building a customer-facing storefront instead? See
            [/docs/store](/docs/store).

            New here? [/guides/admin](/guides/admin) walks through getting a key and calling your first
            endpoint step by step - this page is the field-level reference to come back to afterward.

            ## Getting Started

            1. Click the **Authorize** button at the top of this page.
            2. Provide an **API Key** via header `X-Commerce-Key` or `X-Storefront-Application-Key` - an Admin
               Application Key in the form `sk_admin_{storeRef}_{secret}`. Admin keys are always secret
               (server-to-server only) - there is no publishable admin key, and a request carrying a browser
               `Origin` header is rejected outright regardless of any other credential supplied.

            The key is the whole credential: it identifies the store, so there is no separate store header to
            send, and no token to exchange it for first.

            **Migrating from the unversioned `api/` surface?** That surface also accepts HTTP Basic and a
            Token-scheme JWT. Neither is accepted here. Issue an Admin Application Key for this API and use
            it directly; your existing integration keeps working against `api/` in the meantime.

            Once authorized, you can explore and test all available endpoints directly from this interface.

            ## Errors

            Failures use RFC 9457 Problem Details (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code` field for
            programmatic handling, e.g. `admin_key_not_browser_safe`, `store_ref_invalid`, `unauthorized`.

            ## Rate Limits

            Requests are limited per Application Key (200/minute), falling back to per-IP if no key is
            present. A 429 response includes a `Retry-After` header.

post.summary: Trigger a Solr search reindex for the caller's own store
post.description:
Equivalent to Backoffice's Settings > Search Indexing > Index Products button -
    creates, repairs or rebuilds the store's Solr collection, then indexes its catalogue. By default only
    products that are missing, changed in the last 48 hours or priced differently are sent; pass full=true
    to re-send every product when the index has gone stale. This is a heavier, synchronous operation for a
    large catalogue; call it deliberately rather than on a tight polling loop.

parameters.name: full
parameters.description: Re-send every product rather than only the ones that changed.

200.description: HTTP status 200 if successfully processed, else returns HTTP status 400

    created here.

example a supplier feed) in the import history.

CommitWarning; false rejects the whole file when any row fails. Without it the profile's 'Invalid Rows'
setting applies. Either way GET imports/{id}/results lists every problem, and ErrorsFilePath is a CSV of the
failed rows to fix and upload again.

202 Accepted with a Location header for GET imports/{id}. Poll that until Status is Complete, CommitWarning,

response is 201 with the import id, and the import waits for validate and commit calls as before.
